newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to announce tariff cuts within a few weeks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to announce tariff cuts within a few weeks.

text.p: The Egyptian government, fulfilling a central element in its draft agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), will announce tariff cuts within a few weeks, Minister of State Youssef Boutros-Ghali said on Tuesday.
The cuts will be the first across the board since February 1994, when the maximum tariff rate for goods other than luxuries fell to 70 percent from 80 percent.
The government was to have made another round of cuts by the end of 1994 but negotiations with the IMF made no progress until a new government took office in Egypt in January this year.
Boutros-Ghali told reporters at an investment conference that the cuts would be moderate. He declined to give figures.
"It will be steep enough to induce our industry to start adapting to international criteria for efficiency, competitiveness etc., but not steep enough to destroy our system," he told Reuters.
Tariff cut proposals by the Egyptian government have usually run into stiff opposition from local industrialists, who have traditionally relied on high tariff barriers.

Boutros-Ghali, who is minister of state for economic follow-up, said the government was also working on tax reform but this was not part of the IMF agreement, which will go to the IMF board in Washington on October 11.

"Even though we have agreed on the (IMF) agreement and it's all signed, we still have to formulate this (tax changes). The aim is to align our tax structure, our tax administration with international norms, which means lowering taxation and streamlining," he added.
Egyptian officials say they are confident that the IMF board will approve the agreement, which will clear the way for Egypt's official creditors to write off $4 billion lent to Egypt.

Boutros-Ghali told the conference the government's budget deficit in this financial year would be about one percent of GDP, compared to 1.3 percent in 1995/6 and well within any IMF target. The financial years start on July 1.
He said the government's target for GDP growth this year was five percent, compared with 4.5 percent last year.
But Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri told the same conference that the budget deficit would be 1.3 percent of GDP this year.

As an indication of the government's success in yielding ground to the private sector, Ganzouri said the private sector now accounted for 55 percent of investment and 63 percent of GDP, compared to 15 percent and 40 percent six years ago.
